text.p: Swedish property company Diligentia said on Wednesday it was bidding for rival Hufvudstaden International.
Diligentia said in a statement it was offering Hufvudstaden International shareholders one of its shares in return for 13 in the target company.
Diligentia said it had approval of owners representing 77 percent of share capital and votes in the bid but that it would need approval from 90 percent to carry out the takeover.
"The intention is to divide Diligentia into an international company and a Swedish company which will then be listed separately," Diligentia said.
"Thereby Diligentia creates two large restructured companies with good liquidity in both shares," it said.
The bid represented a 25 percent premium on the average share price of Hufvudstaden International in the past 10 days, it said.
It said the book value of the two companies' international divisions at the end of 1996 totalled 11.6 billion crowns, of which Brussels, Paris and London accounted for 71 percent.
The book value of Swedish properties totalled 10.4 billion crowns at the same time.
It said it intended to build an international property company focused on markets in Brussels, Paris and London combining the two companies' international divisions.
Diligentia said this move was part of its international strategy.
"It gives the possibility for increased activity within Swedish operations as well as more active participation in the ongoing restructuring of the sector in Sweden," it said.
Trade in Hufvudstaden International shares was suspended on the Stockholm Stock Exchange ahead of the bid but resumed at 1245 GMT.
Diligentia traded up 1.5 crowns at 101.5 at 1325 and Hufvudstaden International was down 30 ore at 35.50 crowns.
